slot.brief: Identify the glycosidic linkage and monosaccharide units of sucrose/maltose/lactose and which are reducing — mixed recall with a small reasoning element.

stem: Which option correctly matches a disaccharide with its glycosidic linkage, constituent monosaccharides and reducing character?

verdicts.working: Maltose consists of glucose + glucose linked α(1→4) and is reducing, so B is correct. Lactose contains galactose + glucose; sucrose is nonreducing.

working:
Maltose has an $\alpha(1\to4)$ linkage between two glucose units; one anomeric carbon remains free $\Rightarrow$ reducing.

Independent check: Maltose consists of glucose + glucose linked α(1→4) and is reducing, so B is correct. Lactose contains galactose + glucose; sucrose is nonreducing.
solution: Maltose consists of two glucose units joined by an $\alpha(1\to4)$ glycosidic linkage. One anomeric carbon remains free, so maltose is reducing.
